irremediable

ir-ri-MEE-dee-uh-bul · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Irremediable is not able to be cured or fixed.

The flood had caused irremediable damage to the ancient manuscripts; no amount of restoration work could bring the water-soaked pages back.

Example

The surgeon explained that the nerve damage was irremediable -- physical therapy could help him adapt, but it could never fully repair the nerve itself.

Irremediable describes harm so complete that no treatment, however skilled, can undo it.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

incurable: Incurable is the medical word: a disease or condition that no treatment can cure. Irremediable covers far more than illness — any damage, loss, or harm that nothing can ever put right, from a lost fortune to a friendship past saving.

irreparable: Irreparable means not able to be repaired, and it points at broken things and bonds — an irreparable engine, an irreparable rift. Irremediable is broader and a shade more formal: no remedy of any kind, no repair, cure, or fix, can undo the harm.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

curable: able to be cured

reversible: able to be undone

Where it sits · whether the damage can ever be undone

unfortunate → irremediable → terminal

unfortunate vs. irremediable: Unfortunate is far weaker than irremediable: a stain on a shirt is merely unfortunate, but an irremediable loss can never be washed out or fixed at all.

terminal vs. irremediable: Terminal is graver still than irremediable: irremediable damage can never be undone, yet a person can adapt and live around it, while a terminal condition is carrying its victim toward the end.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ir-: not (Latin)

root+suffix — remediable: able to be remedied (Latin (remedium))

Put it together: ir- ("not") + remediable ("able to be remedied") = beyond any hope of a cure or fix.

Use the root in a new word: remedy: Every Tuesday, Ms. Alvarez stayed late to run the remedial session in Room 12.
